claims.statement: OpenWiki resolves its state/home directory to ~/.openwiki by default (os.homedir() joined with .openwiki), but OPENWIKI_CONFIG_DIR overrides it, with manual tilde expansion because path.resolve does not expand a leading ~.
ensureOpenWikiHome creates the home directory plus its connectors, conversation_history, wiki, and skills subdirectories with owner-only 0o700 permissions.
The persisted environment file lives at <home>/.env (openWikiEnvPath), displayed to users as ~/.openwiki/.env, and openWikiEnvDir equals the resolved home directory.

On Windows, restrictDirToCurrentUser enforces owner-only intent with icacls by granting full control to the current user and the SYSTEM SID (*S-1-5-18) then removing inherited ACEs, because fs.chmod only toggles the read-only attribute on Windows; it is best-effort (returns false instead of throwing) and a no-op on non-Windows platforms.

The state directory is protected by restrictDirToCurrentUser on both directory creation (ensureOpenWikiHome) and env save (saveOpenWikiEnvLocked), applying the Windows ACL restriction alongside the 0o700 mode.

MANAGED_ENV_KEYS is the single source of truth for every env var OpenWiki reads or persists, in file-write order, and both CREDENTIAL_DIAGNOSTIC_ENV_KEYS and DEBUG_ENV_KEYS are derived from it by filtering so they cannot drift out of sync when a new managed key is added; it includes OPENWIKI_BEDROCK_MAX_TOKENS_ENV_KEY alongside the other Bedrock and provider keys.
LangChain project/tracing settings (LANGCHAIN_PROJECT, LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2) are managed but excluded from the credential diagnostics panel via NON_CREDENTIAL_ENV_KEYS.

loadOpenWikiEnv reads ~/.openwiki/.env and copies each value into process.env only when the key is not already set, so a shell export wins over the saved file at runtime; deprecated keys are skipped and a missing file yields an empty map.

OpenWiki keeps two in-memory startup snapshots — the shell's values for managed keys (captureShellEnv/getShellEnvValue, idempotent so the first call wins) and the saved file's values (savedEnvAtStartup/getSavedEnvValue) — both never persisted or logged, so the setup wizard can distinguish shell overrides from saved config.

saveOpenWikiEnv serializes all writes through a promise queue so concurrent saves cannot interleave, and a rejected save is swallowed in the queue chain so it does not permanently block later saves while the caller still receives the original error.

saveOpenWikiEnvLocked writes the env file atomically by writing to a uniquely named temp file (mode 0o600) in the same directory and renaming it into place, avoiding the O_TRUNC data-loss window of a plain writeFile that could truncate ~/.openwiki/.env and lose saved tokens on a mid-write failure.

On save, keys with an empty value are dropped rather than persisted as KEY= (which would read back as configured), deprecated keys are removed, and process.env is updated to mirror the file except for keys whose value came from a shell export at startup, which are left untouched.

formatEnv writes managed keys first in MANAGED_ENV_KEYS order followed by other keys sorted alphabetically, always double-quoting and escaping values via formatEnvValue (which replaces backslash first, then quote, then newline, then carriage-return, in that order for the reverse direction). parseEnv reads them back: it ignores blanks and # comments, accepts an optional export prefix, requires UPPER_SNAKE_CASE keys, and unescapes double-quoted values through parseEnvValue, which performs a single atomic left-to-right pass over /\\(.)/gsu (switch on n/r/quote/backslash, other escaped pairs left intact) rather than sequential replace() calls, preventing a corruption bug where a raw backslash produced by unescaping \\n could be re-read with the next character as a new escape pair (e.g. a Windows path C:\name\creds.json getting its backslash + name read as a newline + ame).
When OPENWIKI_PROVIDER is unset, resolveConfiguredProvider infers the provider from whichever credential env var is present in a fixed check order and falls back to DEFAULT_PROVIDER (openai).

resolveConfiguredMaxOutputTokens resolves the per-request output-token cap in precedence: OPENWIKI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (provider-neutral, positive safe integer) wins when set; otherwise the OpenRouter legacy OPENWIKI_OPENROUTER_MAX_TOKENS takes precedence on openrouter runs, and on bedrock the OPENWIKI_BEDROCK_MAX_TOKENS default (16000 via BEDROCK_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS) applies; otherwise the cap is undefined.

The openai-compatible provider exposes three independent boolean toggles (true only when the value trims to "true"): OPENWIKI_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_USE_RESPONSES_API routes through the Responses API, OPENWIKI_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_STREAMING forces the SSE streaming HTTP transport for gateways that only serve streaming, and OPENWIKI_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_REASONING_EFFORT_SUPPORTED gates whether the provider supports reasoning effort at all.

OPENWIKI_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_STREAM_MESSAGES is a distinct axis from the streaming HTTP transport: it controls how LangGraph surfaces a run in the TUI (the messages stream mode) rather than whether the request is sent as SSE.

OPENWIKI_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT sets the milliseconds to wait for the first or next Bedrock stream chunk and is applied only to the bedrock provider by resolveStreamIdleTimeoutForProvider, with 0 disabling the stream watchdog so stalled streams may hang indefinitely.
OPENWIKI_PROVIDER_RETRY_ATTEMPTS sets provider retry attempts as a positive integer, defaulting to DEFAULT_PROVIDER_RETRY_ATTEMPTS (3) when unset.

OPENWIKI_REASONING_EFFORT accepts one of none/low/medium/high/xhigh/max; resolveReasoningConfig returns undefined when unset but throws for an invalid value, for a provider/model with no reasoning capability, or for a value outside that capability's supported values, and each capability carries the transport used to send it.

getCredentialDiagnostics builds one diagnostic per key reporting its source (process.env, the env file, process.env over the file, or unset), a masked preview for secrets (verbatim via isNonSecretDiagnosticKey for non-secret settings including OPENWIKI_BEDROCK_MAX_TOKENS and all three openai-compatible boolean toggles), and per-key validation warnings through a dedicated validator per key (invalid provider, model, token limits, boolean, reasoning effort, retry attempts, stream idle timeout, base-URL mismatch, or credential formatting, plus a disabled-Bedrock-watchdog warning when the idle timeout is 0).

sanitizeDiagnosticText is the security boundary that redacts secrets before any text is shown or logged: it replaces the exact values of secrets currently set in the environment plus known token shapes (sk- keys, Bearer headers, LangSmith ls tokens, and the Incorrect API key phrasing), and getErrorMessage routes user-facing errors through it.

isSecretLikeKey, backed by the shared SECRET_KEY_PATTERN_SOURCE, is the single source of truth for deciding whether a key name is secret-bearing, so diagnostics, OpenRouter response bodies, and MCP tool args/results all redact the same keys.

resolveBedrockMaxTokens caps Bedrock Converse API output and defaults to BEDROCK_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS (16000) when OPENWIKI_BEDROCK_MAX_TOKENS is unset, because without an explicit maxTokens Bedrock caps output at 4096 and truncates long wiki pages; it throws on any non-positive-safe-integer value.

OPENWIKI_BEDROCK_MAX_TOKENS is a non-secret diagnostic key whose value is shown verbatim and validated by its own getBedrockMaxTokensWarnings validator (calling resolveBedrockMaxTokens and reporting an invalid output token limit on failure), distinct from the neutral getMaxOutputTokensWarnings and the OpenRouter getOpenRouterMaxTokensWarnings validators.

REASONING_CAPABILITIES declares three transports: responses-reasoning (openai and openai-chatgpt GPT-5.6 models, and openai-compatible when the Responses-API opt-in is set) sent as the Responses reasoning.effort payload; chat-completions-reasoning-effort (NVIDIA NIM nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b, and openai-compatible when reasoning effort is opted in but Responses API is not used) sent as the reasoning_effort kwarg; and gemini-thinking-level (gemini-3.6-flash) sent as the Gemini thinkingLevel option. The agent model constructor applies the chosen transport via responsesReasoningOptions, chatCompletionsReasoningOptions, or geminiThinkingLevelOptions respectively.

For the openai-compatible provider, getOpenAiCompatibleReasoningCapability returns undefined unless OPENWIKI_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_REASONING_EFFORT_SUPPORTED is true (so resolveReasoningConfig throws 'not supported' without the opt-in); when opted in it selects responses-reasoning when OPENWIKI_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_USE_RESPONSES_API is set, otherwise chat-completions-reasoning-effort, and supports the full REASONING_EFFORT_VALUES set either way.

Reasoning capability value sets are per transport/model: openai and openai-chatgpt GPT-5.6 models and opted-in openai-compatible support the full none/low/medium/high/xhigh/max set, gemini-3.6-flash supports only low/medium/high, and NVIDIA NIM nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b supports only none/low/high, so a value like max is rejected for Gemini and NVIDIA models even though valid for OpenAI GPT-5.6.

OPENWIKI_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_REASONING_EFFORT_SUPPORTED is a managed key (listed in MANAGED_ENV_KEYS), a non-secret diagnostic key (shown verbatim in the diagnostics panel via isNonSecretDiagnosticKey), and validated as a boolean by getBooleanWarnings alongside the other two openai-compatible toggles, reporting 'invalid boolean' for any value not trimming to true or false.

.openwikiignore (OPENWIKI_IGNORE_FILE) is a gitignore-style read boundary at the repository root that OpenWikiIgnore.load reads; a missing file is an inactive matcher (isActive false) and any non-missing-file read error is rethrown rather than fail-open. It scopes agent filesystem/shell access, not a guarantee a topic is never mentioned.

.openwikiignore syntax supports blank/#-comment lines (dropped), * (single segment), ? (one non-slash char), **/ (zero+ leading dirs) and trailing ** (nested), leading-/ or embedded-slash anchoring to repo root, trailing-/ directory scoping (still matches nested files), and ! negation with last-match-wins in file order.

.openwikiignore matching is case-insensitive (i flag) everywhere and canonicalizes paths via normalizeIgnorePath (backslashes to slashes, . / .. collapsed by path.posix.normalize) so equivalent spellings like ./secrets/token.txt or secrets/../secrets/token.txt cannot bypass an anchored rule on case-insensitive filesystems.

OpenWikiLocalShellBackend enforces .openwikiignore on every agent tool: read/readRaw/write/edit/delete hard-deny ignored paths with an error, ls/glob/grep silently drop ignored entries and short-circuit when the search root is ignored, upload/download return permission_denied for ignored paths while processing allowed ones, and shell execute is restricted to the allowedIgnoredShellCommands allowlist (pwd and git rev-parse HEAD) while any rule is active because arbitrary shell cannot be proven not to read an ignored path.

openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md (REPOSITORY_INSTRUCTIONS_FILE) is a user-authored Markdown brief for the repository wiki's scope/priorities that OpenWiki reads via readRepositoryWikiInstructions and threads into the run as wikiGoal, but never rewrites during normal runs; openwiki --init preserves it while replacing the rest of the generated wiki and Claims, and a non-empty wikiGoal is required for onboarding to be complete.

In local-wiki/personal mode the equivalent user brief lives in the private state directory at ~/.openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md (openWikiInstructionsPath, mode 0o600 written by saveOpenWikiOnboardingConfig) and is read by readWikiInstructions, distinct from the committed repository openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md (mode 0o644 written by saveRepositoryWikiInstructions).

openwiki/.langsmith.json (getLangSmithRepoConfigPath) is a committed JSON config read by the LangSmith connector that names workspaces and projects to document but never the API key: each workspace carries an apiKeyEnv (the env-var name, constrained to the OPENWIKI_LANGSMITH_API_KEY(_<n>) namespace by sanitizeLangSmithApiKeyEnv) and optional apiBaseUrl (validated against the three official LangSmith hosts by sanitizeLangSmithApiBaseUrl, since the base URL receives the key as an Authorization header); the key itself lives in ~/.openwiki/.env or a CI secret.

parseLangSmithRepoConfig reads only named, allowlisted fields and drops any workspace failing a shape or allowlist (apiKeyEnv/apiBaseUrl) check rather than failing the whole config, so a malicious committed config cannot point the connector at an arbitrary host or name an unrelated secret as the key to send. The setup wizard writes it WYSIWYG via saveLangSmithSetup/writeLangSmithRepoConfig only once the LangSmith sub-menu is opened (langsmithSourcesTouched), so an untouched setup never rewrites the file.
